relationship: Editing, translating and running pseudocode or Python connects corresponding statements to execution state and diagnostics.

learnerLoop.action: Load or edit code, choose a view, then step or run the selected language.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The source, translated counterpart and runtime execution state change.
learnerLoop.evidence: The paired editors, health indicators, console, variables and diagnostics show the result.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Correct the source or compare the equivalent statement in the other language.

invariants: Translation and runtime feedback refer to the currently displayed source.
Stepping exposes execution one statement at a time.
safeAdaptations: Change example programs, terminology or guidance while retaining paired code representation and execution evidence.
nonGoals: Providing a general-purpose compiler or unrestricted Python runtime.

task.description: Compare the two program representations and their execution.
task.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

controls.description: Edit either language, load examples, select structural matching, step/run and supply input.
controls.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

model.description: Paired editable pseudocode and Python with syntax highlights and aligned line numbers.
model.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

evidence.description: Translation health, execution output, variables and current runtime state.
evidence.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

source.description: Current source text and its translated counterpart.

runtime-input.description: Input requested by the active program.
runtime-input.domain: Text accepted by the current INPUT/input operation.

modes.views: Pseudocode, Both and Python; swapping editor positions and resizing panes remain available.
modes.translation: Match pseudocode structure retains the corresponding structural representation; switching it changes Python presentation.
modes.execution: Step, Run, Stop, Restart and speed selection operate on the active language; Console/Variables and light/dark scheme are retained.

dependencies: Editing one language updates the counterpart and its translation status.
Execution, line highlights and variable/console evidence refer to the active program.
Editor input, highlighting and gutter share 14px/24px metrics. Model-specific splitters and interpreter remain intact.
implementation.completion: Open programming workbench; no completion gate or Working levels.
limitations: Custom supported translation/interpreter subset, not a general-purpose compiler or unrestricted Python environment.
